t: Section 10(d) of the Federal Power Act, as amended (16 U.S.C. 803), is amended by adding at the end thereof the following: “For any new license issued under section 15, the amortization reserves under this subsection shall lie maintained on and after the effective date of such new license.”

fable.w: This amendment only specifies when amortization reserves must be maintained for new licenses under the Federal Power Act. The mention of a "license" might suggest outside-party involvement, but licensing is an application-type process and the text creates no consultation, hearing, comment, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: For any new license issued under section 15, the amortization reserves under this subsection shall lie maintained on and after the effective date of such new license.

qwen_block.w: This section mandates the maintenance of financial amortization reserves for new licenses. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or tribes) in the decision-making process. The text is purely administrative and financial in nature.
qwen_block.s: For any new license issued under section 15, the amortization reserves under this subsection shall lie maintained on and after the effective date of such new license.

opus.w: The amendment only sets an accounting rule: amortization reserves continue to be maintained under new licenses. It creates no comment period, hearing, consultation with outside parties, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The reference to a license is not participation, because licensing is excluded under the definition, and here the text doesn't even describe an application process.
opus.s: For any new license issued under section 15, the amortization reserves under this subsection shall lie maintained on and after the effective date of such new license.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The mention of a "new license issued under section 15" of the Federal Power Act might look like a process involving outside licensees. But the definition excludes license applications, and this amendment doesn't even describe an application process. It only says that amortization reserves must continue after a new license takes effect. No comment period, hearing, consultation, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue is created. Only federal actors and existing licensees are involved, and there is no outside input into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a financial requirement on licensees regarding amortization reserves. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from any outside party (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The text describes a condition of the license itself, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: For any new license issued under section 15, the amortization reserves under this subsection shall lie maintained on and after the effective date of such new license.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because this is an amendment to a statute governing licenses, it implies a process where outside parties (license applicants) participate. However, the text itself only mandates a financial accounting rule ("amortization reserves... shall be maintained"). It does not describe any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory role for non-federal entities. It is a substantive regulatory requirement, not a procedural participation mechanism.
